one_month_reasoning: No TT earnings in the window (Q4 results late January 2027). In the window: the ~$256M debenture put settlement in November (no material election, 10-Q), Nvidia's quarterly results in the second half of November (AI data-center sentiment; the January Vera Rubin 'no chillers' remark cost TT 4-8% in a day), and macro prints. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: a guidance-driven sell-off after a beat (-8.6% from $448.47 to $410) tends to drift, but a sharp two-day drop on a reaffirmed guide also mean-reverts. Net: centred on $410 with ~9% monthly sigma (30%/3.5 = 8.6%, nudged up for the Nvidia event) and slightly fat tails.

fair_value.method: Quarterly segment driver build to FY2028 valued at the horizon on NTM GAAP EPS x 21.31x P/E (75%) and NTM EBITDA x 15.55x EV/EBITDA (25%), less asbestos at expected value: P/E leg $395.23, EV/EBITDA leg $388.74, blend $393.61. Our FY2027/FY2028 EPS sit 1.3%/5.4% below Street on flatter margins.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. The Q3 2026 print beat ($4.86 vs $4.74) but the beat was tax-driven (17.3% adjusted ETR vs 21.3%; at 20% EPS ~4.69), Q3's guided +50bp margin came in -40bp, full-year price was cut to ~1pt and organic leverage to 'low 20s', and the reaffirmed $15.20-15.30 implies Q4 $3.40-3.50 vs a pre-print Street ~$3.64 - hence -8.6% on the 'beat'. Cash flow is flattered: customer deposits +$835M and supplier finance +$148M YTD (FCF conversion 108%; ~76% ex-deposits). Americas book-to-bill fell to 101% from ~150% in Q1, and >$8B of the $12.5B backlog ships in 2027+ but only >$1B in 2028, so 2028 depends on new data-center orders while Bernstein sees 35-40% of announced capacity at risk of delay/cancellation and Nvidia's warm-water cooling questions chiller content. Insiders sold (CEO 48,091 shares at $480 on 10/6, CFO at $450 in April, both 10b5-1); short interest is low (1.6% of float), credit is strong (Moody's A3, outlook positive) and the asbestos court estimate ($742.5M) exceeds the $545M plan. Weighing it honestly: revenue visibility for 2027 is real (we are slightly above Street on FY2027 revenue), so the downside case is about margins and the multiple, not a collapse. Build: 6 drivers by quarter; FY26 24.2B/18.0% GAAP EBIT margin, FY27 26.4B/18.4%, FY28 28.1B/18.8% vs Street EBIT margin ~20.4% (adjusted) in FY28; FY27 EPS ~17.5 adjusted vs Street 17.71 / whisper 18.10; FY28 ~19.3 GAAP vs 20.41. Exit P/E 21.31x from peer median 18.3x with k=0.8 shrink less 1.25x long-dated risk; EV/EBITDA cross-check 15.55x. Research target (12m) $393.61 (~4% below $410); downside case $270.3 (data-center pause, -250bp margins, -3 turns), upside case $522.93. Source mix: 13 of 32 sources are skeptic-lane (litigation/credit notes in the 10-Q, short interest, insider sales, downgrade history, Bernstein cancellations, Nvidia cooling reports, bear-case pieces); the other 19 are company releases, transcripts and consensus pages used for the brief's exempt basic facts (segment quarters, guidance record, consensus). All legs are driver-linked; no custom per-share legs.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The k=0.8 rule keeps ~1.23x of TT's 1.30x premium (higher returns on capital, applied/data-center mix, A3 credit with positive outlook). We do not argue any further premium: margins fell y/y in each 2026 quarter and the premium's persistence depends on a data-center cycle with 35-40% of announced capacity at risk of delay/cancellation (Bernstein). The 1.25x haircut is the probability-weighted long-dated risk (see long_dated_risks).

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led quarterly segment build (Americas, EMEA, Asia Pacific; 6 drivers: segment revenue and GAAP segment operating margin; corporate expense a cited constant) covering 100% of revenue, reproducing FY2025 exactly (21,321.9 revenue, 3,967.4 EBIT) and the three reported 2026 quarters. Value carried by an NTM P/E horizon leg (0.75) on the build's own GAAP EPS and an NTM EV/EBITDA cross-check (0.25); no DCF (policy), no SOTP (not a conglomerate). Asbestos adjustments at expected value. Backlog conversion ($12.5B, >$8B for 2027+, >$1B for 2028) is applied in the Americas revenue path rather than as a separate driver because TT does not disclose segment backlog.
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) the 1.25x long-dated-risk haircut on the exit P/E moves the research target (12m) by ~-5.5% (~$23/share; without it ~$417) - judgment, flagged. (2) Our model EPS is GAAP (after acquired-backlog amortization ~$0.07/qtr), slightly below the adjusted EPS the peer multiples use (~1%), conservative. (3) No financing event >=20% probability: no ATM/convert/shelf usage; ~$256M debenture puts in Nov 2026 with no material election (10-Q), covered by cash. (4) fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value.
